A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Alt-MoE, with matching core equations, architecture and retained retrieval results. All material supports comparison. V1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes four pages of supplementary material, which were also inspected.

before.justification: V1 reports original COCO/Flickr30K retrieval results, alignment-objective and architecture ablations, and loss-weight sensitivity results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 4.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds audio retrieval, VQA/NLVR-2, image classification, encoder fine-tuning ablations, retrieval timing and similarity visualization.

M1.justification: The core alternating alignment, cross-embeddings, MoE connector and losses are retained. V2 adds limited downstream adaptations: joint image/question feature aggregation into a 3,129-answer classifier and fusion of frozen DINOv2/CLIP representations followed by a classification head (Sections 5.4–5.5). Newly disclosed routing configurations do not establish changes to the retained retrieval method.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates image-text retrieval on COCO and Flickr30K; its audio experiments are explicitly unfinished. V2 adds Clotho/AudioCaps audio-text retrieval, using WavText5K and Freesound as additional training sources, plus VQA v2, NLVR-2 visual reasoning and ImageNet-1K classification. The original image-text coverage remains.

E2.justification: The comparator set in image-text Table 1 is unchanged. V2 adds audio comparisons with AVFIC, ImageBind, VALOR and LanguageBind; VQA/NLVR-2 comparisons including X-VLM, SimVLM, CoCa and ONE-PEACE; classification comparisons with CLIP-ViT and DINOv2; and a separate retrieval-timing comparison with CLIP.

E3.justification: The original Flickr30K 1K and COCO 5K retrieval settings remain. Added studies introduce held-out audio dataset protocols, COCO alignment followed by VQA classification, ImageNet linear probing, and frozen/partial/full-layer LoRA controls. Appendix 1.2.4 also reports random, adaptive and sequential task-selection protocols. Specifying the final three LoRA layers clarifies an existing setting rather than demonstrating its revision.

E4.justification: The original objective and MoE/alternation ablations are retained, and the loss-weight analysis moves to Appendix 1.3. V2 adds an encoder-freezing versus partial/full LoRA ablation, a qualitative comparison of task-selection strategies, a CLIP retrieval-efficiency analysis and a similarity-matrix case study using ten COCO image-text pairs.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, reports confidence intervals or error bars, or presents statistical significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V1 Tables 1–3 match v2 Tables 1, 4 and 5, and the sensitivity curves are unchanged. New results include Clotho text-to-audio R@1 of 20.1 versus LanguageBind's 15.5, ImageNet accuracy of 86.6% versus DINOv2's 83.2%, and VQA test-dev/test-std scores of 82.3/82.5. Appendix results add NLVR-2, timing and full-layer LoRA outcomes; the latter are additional configurations, not improvements under the original setting.

T1.justification: The alignment decomposition, information-theoretic objective, alternating updates and prediction/contrastive loss equations are substantively unchanged. V2 duplicates the encoding definition as Equations 6 and 7 and renumbers subsequent equations. It adds no formal theorem, proof, assumption or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: V1 presents world modeling as a future goal; v2's introduction makes building a hierarchical world model and abstracting complex dependencies a present contribution. The abstract adds explicit VQA and unseen-data generalization claims and describes scaling through changes in MoE capacity and expert activation, whereas v1 emphasizes scaling without architecture changes.

C2.justification: V2 attributes performance to hierarchical expert specialization and abstract reasoning, expanding beyond v1's representation-convergence explanation. Appendix 1.7 explicitly limits current alignment to two modalities and discusses VQA difficulties with spatial relationships and global context. The generative-task limitation is retained. Appendix 1.3 also adds an inaccurate interpretation describing the unchanged contrastive-weight curve as steadily improving.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands implementation disclosure: LanguageBind encoder fine-tuning, task-specific expert counts, top-k routing, hidden widths, dropout, omission of load-balancing loss, linear probing and the final-three-layer LoRA setting. V1 supplies much less operational detail. However, v2 omits v1's code/checkpoint access URL; this establishes removal of the access pointer, not withdrawal of the resources themselves.

R1.justification: V1 explicitly positions Alt-MoE as JEPA/I-JEPA-based and discusses its relationship to Assran et al.; v2 removes that discussion and citation. Positioning shifts toward direct versus unidirectional alignment and hierarchical world modeling, with added discussion or citations involving ImageBind, VLMo, LanguageBind and LeCun's world-model agenda. Additional references support the expanded experiments.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, five contribution statements become two, and result explanations and the conclusion are revised. Sensitivity analysis and limitations are reorganized into supplementary material. V2 also introduces a duplicated Image and Text Encoding subsection in Sections 4.1 and 4.2.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is replaced by a three-framework comparison, Figure 2 receives an expanded caption, and retained tables are resized and relocated. V2 adds task and LoRA tables, a timing bar chart and a similarity heatmap. The existing sensitivity plot moves to the appendix without changing its curves.

improvement.justification: V1 claims broad task and modality scalability while reporting only image-text retrieval and leaving audio results pending. V2 supplies audio, VQA/NLVR-2 and classification evidence, substantially addressing that central validation gap. Its implementation disclosures and encoder fine-tuning controls also make the findings more assessable. Stronger world-model claims remain untested, the new sensitivity interpretation misreads the retained plot, and the code access pointer disappears. These drawbacks temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial improvement in empirical support and documentation.
